title: Zanzibar Samosa
community: Zanzibar Stone Town — the coastal samosa tradition
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Zanzibar Sambusa — thin crispy pastry filled with spiced minced beef or vegetables, folded into triangles and deep-fried golden. The Zanzibari version of the samosa — thinner, crispier pastry and more elaborately spiced than the Indian original.
longDesc: Zanzibar sambusa arrived through Indian Ocean trade routes and was transformed by the island's spice heritage. The pastry is thinner and crispier than Indian samosa, and the filling uses the full Zanzibar spice array. Sold at every market, eaten at every celebration.
steps: Make pastry: combine flour, salt, oil, water. Knead 5 minutes. Rest 20 minutes.
Cook filling: brown minced beef with onion, garlic, ginger, chilli, spices. Cook until dry. Add coriander. Cool.
Roll pastry very thin. Cut into rectangles.
Fold each rectangle into a cone. Fill with meat. Fold top to seal triangle.
Seal edges with a paste of flour and water.
Fry in batches 3—4 minutes until golden and crispy.
Serve with chatni ya Nazi and pili pili.
chefTips: Filling must be completely cool and dry before filling — moisture makes pastry soggy.
Seal edges carefully — oil entering ruins them.
cookingScience: See KEN230 for samosa/sambusa pastry cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: The Indian Ocean trade route food that is now completely Tanzanian.
storage: Freeze uncooked 2 months. Fry from frozen.
culturalNote: Zanzibar sambusa is the Indian Ocean trade made edible — the pastry technique from India, the beef and spice filling transformed by Zanzibar, the result belonging entirely to the island.
